note: OpeningHours decided by hand, where OpenStreetMap carried no usable opening_hours tag. Every row states the basis it rests on. Values here are not OSM-derived and carry no ODbL obligation, which is why they live in their own file rather than in opening-hours.osm.json.
_comment: Three bases, because the hand-work has three genuinely different outcomes:
"sourced"      a real opening time read off a published page. Requires
`openingHours`, `source` (URL) and `retrieved` (ISO date),
so a thesis reader can go and check it.
"always-open"  genuinely unconstrained — a square, a park, a street, an
open viewpoint. Requires a `rationale` and NO openingHours:
the value is always 24/7 and the loader supplies it. There
is no page to cite for "this fountain has no gates", and
demanding a URL would only produce a fabricated citation.
"unknown"      looked at, and deliberately left unknown. Requires a
`rationale` and resolves to no value at all. This exists so
that "we checked and there is nothing to record" is visible
as a decision — an attraction simply missing from this file
is indistinguishable from one nobody has examined yet.
CONTEXT.md's OpeningHours entry is what these bases protect: "always open"
is a fact about the attraction, "unknown" is a fact about our data, and the
two must never be conflated.
Names must match attractions.json exactly — the loader rejects orphans, and
an attraction claimed by both this file and the OSM one is an error rather
than a precedence rule.
PH/SH holiday macros must not be stored: measured 2026-08-09 they throw for
`tr` and `gb` (Istanbul, London). Rewrite them to explicit dates and record
the original in `rewrittenFrom` so the transformation stays auditable.
Progress is counted by scripts/attraction-data-coverage.ts, which writes
docs/research/attraction-data-coverage.md — the methodology note. Tracked as
issue #25.

entries.rationale: A public pedestrian street and the square it ends at. Continuously accessible; individual shops along it keep their own hours, but the attraction as visited is the street itself.
An open-air street site at the Friedrichstraße crossing — the reconstructed guardhouse and signage stand in the public roadway. The adjacent private museum is ticketed, but it is not this attraction.
A public square. The concert hall and cathedrals framing it keep their own hours; the square itself is never closed.
A public square at the end of Andrássy Avenue, open on all sides and continuously accessible.
An open-air fountain in a public piazza, with no enclosure and no admission.
A public stairway between Piazza di Spagna and Trinità dei Monti. Continuously accessible; sitting on the steps is policed, but access is not.
A public square. Its fountains and the surrounding cafés are visited from the open piazza, which has no closing time.
A public pedestrian boulevard. The market and venues along it keep their own hours; the promenade itself is never closed.
